title: Donepezil for dementia due to Alzheimer's disease
conclusion: Donepezil produces small benefits in cognitive function, activities of daily living and global clinical state in people with mild, moderate or severe dementia due to Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Background: Donepezil is a centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease. Objectives: To assess the clinical efficacy and safety of donepezil in people with mild, moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease. Main results: Thirty trials with a total of 8257 participants met the inclusion criteria. Participants receiving donepezil for 24 weeks scored significantly better on cognitive function (ADAS-Cog mean difference -2.67 points, 95% CI -3.31 to -2.02, P < 0.00001) and global clinical state (CIBIC-plus) compared to placebo. Treatment benefits were observed across mild, moderate and severe disease stages. The most common adverse effects were gastrointestinal (nausea, diarrhoea).

title: Long-term donepezil treatment in 565 patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD2000): randomised double-blind trial
conclusion: Donepezil is associated with modest improvements in cognitive and daily living functions over 2-3 years, but differences in institutionalisation or progression to disability were not statistically significant.
abstract: Background: Cholinesterase inhibitors improve cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease in short-term trials, but their longer term efficacy in delaying institutionalisation and severe disability has not been clearly established. Methods: 565 community-resident patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease were randomly assigned to donepezil (5 mg or 10 mg daily) or placebo. Primary endpoints were entry to institutional care and progression to disability. Findings: Donepezil produced consistent, small improvements in cognitive function and activities of daily living over 2 years, though no significant differences were observed in institutionalisation rates.

title: Memantine for dementia
conclusion: Memantine has a small beneficial effect on cognition, functional capacity, and global clinical state in patients with moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease, but is not beneficial in mild Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Background: Memantine is an uncompetitive, low-affinity N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist. Objectives: To determine the efficacy and safety of memantine in people with Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia and other forms of dementia. Main results: 44 studies with 10,232 participants were included. In moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease, memantine was associated with a small statistically significant benefit on cognition (SMD 0.24, 95% CI 0.17 to 0.32) and activities of daily living (SMD 0.16, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.24). Memantine is well tolerated with adverse event incidence comparable to placebo.

title: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of medications for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in children, adolescents, and adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
conclusion: Methylphenidate should be preferred as first-line pharmacological treatment for children and adolescents with ADHD, balancing robust efficacy with favourable tolerability.
abstract: Background: Guidelines recommend pharmacotherapy for ADHD, but the comparative efficacy and tolerability of available medications remain debated. Methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind randomised controlled trials evaluating ADHD medications in children/adolescents and adults. Findings: Analysis of 133 trials (24,188 participants) showed that methylphenidate was the most efficacious and best-tolerated drug in children and adolescents (SMD -0.78, 95% CI -0.93 to -0.62 for core ADHD symptoms evaluated by teachers).

title: Methylphenidate for children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
conclusion: Methylphenidate improves teacher-reported ADHD core symptoms and general behaviour, though non-serious adverse effects (appetite suppression, sleep disturbance) require monitoring.
abstract: Background: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood psychiatric disorder. Objectives: To evaluate the beneficial and adverse effects of methylphenidate in children and adolescents with ADHD. Main results: 185 randomised trials with 12,245 participants were analysed. Methylphenidate was associated with substantial reductions in teacher-rated ADHD symptoms (SMD -0.77, 95% CI -0.90 to -0.64) and parent-rated symptoms, with low risk of serious adverse events.

title: Modafinil as a cognitive enhancer in healthy non-sleep-deprived subjects: a systematic review
conclusion: Modafinil reliably enhances executive function, memory retrieval and attention in sleep-deprived conditions, and complex planning and decision-making in non-sleep-deprived individuals.
abstract: Background: Modafinil is approved for narcolepsy, shift work sleep disorder and obstructive sleep apnoea. Off-label use as a cognitive enhancer in healthy adults has expanded significantly. Methods: Systematic review of randomized placebo-controlled trials assessing cognitive performance across multiple domains. Findings: Modafinil consistently improved cognitive domains involving working memory, visual pattern recognition, spatial planning, and reaction time under time constraints, without eliciting pronounced hyperlocomotion or euphoria.

title: Modafinil for cognitive neuroenhancement in healthy non-sleep-deprived subjects: A systematic review
conclusion: Systematic evaluation demonstrates that modafinil selectively enhances higher-order cognitive tasks involving executive function, cognitive flexibility, and learning with minimal tolerability concerns.
abstract: Background: Concerns regarding the true efficacy of nootropics necessitate comprehensive evaluation of double-blind evidence. Methods: Literature search identified 24 placebo-controlled studies on non-sleep-deprived healthy individuals between 1990 and 2014. Results: Modafinil enhanced attention, executive function, and learning in 70% of complex cognitive paradigms, with side effects limited to mild headache, nausea, and mild anxiety.

title: Bupropion for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults
conclusion: Bupropion provides statistically significant improvements in ADHD symptoms in adult patients compared with placebo, serving as an effective non-stimulant alternative.
abstract: Background: Bupropion is a dual norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI). Objectives: To evaluate the efficacy and adverse effects of bupropion for ADHD in adults. Main results: Six randomised trials with 438 participants were included. Bupropion significantly reduced ADHD symptom severity compared to placebo (standardised mean difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.66 to -0.17) with low risk of treatment discontinuation due to adverse events.

title: Antidepressants for smoking cessation
conclusion: Bupropion substantially increases long-term smoking cessation rates (relative risk 1.60) compared to placebo.
abstract: Background: Bupropion was the first non-nicotine agent demonstrated to aid smoking cessation. Objectives: To determine whether antidepressant medications aid long-term tobacco cessation. Main results: 46 trials of bupropion (17,866 participants) showed that bupropion significantly increased smoking abstinence at 6 months or longer (RR 1.60, 95% CI 1.49 to 1.72).

title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of 21 antidepressant drugs for the treatment of adults with major depressive disorder: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
conclusion: Sertraline, escitalopram, and vortioxetine demonstrated the most favourable balance between clinical efficacy and acceptability across adult patients with major depressive disorder.
abstract: Background: The comparative efficacy and acceptability of antidepressants in major depressive disorder has been controversial. Methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind randomised trials of 21 antidepressants. Findings: In 522 trials involving 116,477 participants, all antidepressants were more efficacious than placebo. In terms of both efficacy (OR 1.67) and acceptability/dropout rates (OR 0.88), sertraline was identified as a first-line drug of choice.

title: Efficacy of ketamine and esketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis
conclusion: Both intravenous racemic ketamine and intranasal esketamine produce rapid and robust antidepressant and antisuicidal responses in treatment-resistant depression.
abstract: Importance: Ketamine and esketamine represent a novel glutamate NMDA receptor mechanistic paradigm in psychiatry. Objective: To compare the efficacy and safety of racemic ketamine and esketamine for major depression. Data Sources: Systematic search of PubMed and Cochrane databases through 2020. Results: 24 trials (1877 participants) demonstrated rapid symptom reduction at 24 hours (Hedges g = 0.82 for racemic ketamine; g = 0.49 for esketamine) and sustained response at 28 days.

title: Metformin as first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease prevention: a systematic review
conclusion: Metformin significantly reduces all-cause mortality, cardiovascular events, and microvascular complications in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
abstract: Background: Metformin remains the undisputed first-line pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes. Methods: Meta-analysis of randomised trials evaluating metformin against other oral antidiabetic agents and lifestyle intervention. Results: Metformin decreased glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) by 1.1% on average and was associated with significant reductions in cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.94) and myocardial infarction.

title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity
journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
conclusion: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide was associated with sustained, clinically relevant reduction in body weight (-14.9%) and improvement in cardiometabolic risk factors.
abstract: Background: Obesity is a chronic disease requiring potent pharmacological therapies. Methods: In a double-blind trial, 1961 adults with a BMI of 30 or greater were randomly assigned to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (2.4 mg) or placebo for 68 weeks. Results: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was -14.9% in the semaglutide group as compared with -2.4% with placebo (P < 0.001). Semaglutide also improved physical functioning and cardiometabolic markers.

title: Piracetam: a review of its pharmacology and clinical applications in cortical myoclonus, cognitive impairment and dementia
conclusion: Piracetam exhibits neuroprotective and hemorheological properties with established clinical benefit in cortical myoclonus and cerebrovascular cognitive deficits.
abstract: Background: Piracetam is the prototype nootropic agent. Methods: Comprehensive review of pharmacological mechanisms (AMPA allosteric modulation, membrane fluidity restoration) and clinical trials in myoclonus and cognitive impairment. Results: Meta-analyses demonstrated statistically significant efficacy in treating cortical myoclonus and modest benefits in mild cognitive disorders of vascular origin with high safety profile.

title: Effects of caffeine on cognitive performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
conclusion: Caffeine significantly improves reaction time, vigilance, psychomotor speed, and subjective alertness, particularly under conditions of fatigue or sustained attention.
abstract: Background: Caffeine is the most widely consumed adenosine receptor antagonist psychostimulant worldwide. Methods: Meta-analysis of double-blind placebo-controlled trials measuring cognitive function after acute caffeine consumption. Results: Analysis of 40 trials revealed robust effect sizes on simple reaction time (Hedges g = 0.41), choice reaction time (g = 0.38), vigilance, and psychomotor speed.

title: Meta-analysis: melatonin for the treatment of primary sleep disorders
conclusion: Melatonin statistically significantly reduces sleep onset latency, increases total sleep time, and improves overall sleep quality in primary sleep disorders.
abstract: Background: Melatonin has been evaluated extensively for insomnia. Methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised placebo-controlled trials. Results: 19 studies involving 1683 participants met inclusion criteria. Melatonin demonstrated statistically significant reductions in sleep latency (mean difference 7.06 minutes, P < 0.001) and increases in total sleep duration (mean difference 8.25 minutes) with minimal adverse effects.

title: Pregabalin for acute and chronic pain in adults - an overview of Cochrane Reviews
conclusion: Pregabalin demonstrates substantial pain relief (at least 50% pain intensity reduction) in patients with diabetic neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, and central neuropathic pain.
abstract: Background: Pregabalin binds the alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels. Objectives: To assess the analgesic efficacy and adverse events of pregabalin across painful conditions. Main results: Evidence from 45 studies (11,926 participants) demonstrates high-quality evidence of benefit in postherpetic neuralgia and painful diabetic neuropathy.

title: Fluoxetine versus other types of pharmacotherapy for depression
conclusion: Fluoxetine is as effective as other SSRIs and tricyclics in treating depression, with superior patient acceptability and lower discontinuation rates compared to older tricyclic agents.
abstract: Background: Fluoxetine was the first modern selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor. Objectives: To evaluate the comparative efficacy and acceptability of fluoxetine in depressive disorder. Main results: 171 randomised controlled trials (25,000+ participants) showed equivalent antidepressant efficacy between fluoxetine and comparison agents, with significantly fewer dropouts due to adverse events compared to tricyclic antidepressants (OR 0.78).

title: Escitalopram in the treatment of major depressive disorder: a review of efficacy, safety, and patient-reported outcomes
conclusion: Escitalopram demonstrates high selectivity for the serotonin transporter, rapid onset of clinical response, and superior remission rates in major depressive disorder.
abstract: Background: Escitalopram is the pure S-enantiomer of citalopram. Methods: Systematic appraisal of double-blind randomised active-controlled trials comparing escitalopram to other SSRIs and SNRIs. Results: Meta-analyses show superior overall response and remission rates for escitalopram over citalopram and other SSRIs, with high safety and low drug-drug interaction risk.
